competition.flat_book_pnl: A flat seat has zero net financing/competition P&L: paper NAV earning SOFR is benchmarked at SOFR, so those flows cancel, and shocked-risk financing is zero.
competition.funding_basis: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 is the zero-return competition benchmark, not free alpha. Every seat has $100m paper NAV that may be described as earning SOFR, but that capital is equally funded/benchmarked at SOFR so those flows cancel. Deployed shocked-risk capital pays the same official SOFR on trusted standard-shock risk capital: the absolute MTM loss from a 1% adverse spot move, a 100bp (1 percentage point) adverse outright rate move, or a 100bp adverse curve/RV spread move under the trusted duration-1 P&L convention. Equal risk capital receives equal financing treatment across asset classes. Notional is descriptive, not the funding base. A completely flat book — including no-trade-skeptic — therefore has zero net financing/competition P&L from SOFR cash or funding economics. Positive financing/carry alpha requires an explicit markable strategy that earns above SOFR or funds below SOFR. Weekends and holidays carry the last applicable published fixing until the next fixing. If official fixing history cannot be established, new funding accrual fails closed and prior canonical balances are preserved.
competition.instruction: Do not optimize for gross notional or fill available capacity. Size risk from plausible adverse paths and historical excursions while staying inside the trusted risk-capital and drawdown limits. Flat cash at SOFR is the zero benchmark, not a source of alpha. The no-trade-skeptic must include a structured funding_view on every new risk or NO_TRADE thesis: the frozen official SOFR fixing, the relevant SR3 forward-curve view, its own assessment of whether realized funding will print higher, lower, or about the same as the curve, and the implication for remaining at the zero SOFR benchmark versus paying SOFR on shocked-risk capital.
competition.objective: Finish with the highest cumulative net paper P&L across the 14 standing seats.

research_supplement.summary: Overnight markets lean into a higher-for-longer US rate story while equity indices stay elevated and volatility remains subdued. The ten-year Treasury reached its highest level since 2002 alongside a steep two-to-ten-year spread, even as headlines describe gold steadying on cooler US inflation competing with rising yields. Brent near 103.53 and WTI at 90.42 keep energy firm despite talk of Middle East flows normalizing; spot gold near 4186.70 holds at an elevated plateau. The euro trades at multiyear weakness into European inflation concerns and global yield pressure, with the S&P near 7651.54 and Nasdaq near 26861.06 still absorbing the move. Canada's dollar sits rich versus the US dollar, while the yen has firmed near 157 after the Bank of Japan's late-September hike. Watch whether long-end Treasury momentum extends, European FX weakness broadens, and UK and Swiss inflation feed policy expectations.

causal.assumptions_right: Risk assets stayed complacent, so the close did not wait for a growth break that never printed. The 4.91 strip did not rally, which was consistent with hiking not being cancelled. Exiting once the expression was recognized as anti-defensive, and while AU was blocked, capped the damage to unchanged marks plus a limited dollar loss.
causal.assumptions_wrong_or_underweighted: The 56bp cash-to-strip gap was read as slowdown mispricing rather than a path that cash could close from below. Demand failure was unverified and then cash hiked 25bp. A receive of a hike-priced strip is a fade of tightening, which conflicted with a defensive remit while VIX and equities stayed bid. Composition of the -12718.75 on a flat mark is not in the packet (carry, roll, or friction).
causal.causal_divergence: The thesis needed the strip to come in as demand failed. Adjustment came from cash rising toward 4.91, not from 4.91 falling. Same mark, negative P&L, tighter cash: the receive was on the wrong side of delivered tightening.
causal.future_implication: Do not treat the now-eligible AU strip at 4.91 versus cash 4.60 as a green light to rebuild the receive. Remaining hike premium is small, and the expression is still a fade of tightening. Defensive duration belongs where tightening is already extreme in the cash long end, not in STIR strips that still price hikes above cash while risk assets are calm.
causal.observed_reality: The strip exited at the same 4.91 mark, realized P&L was -12718.75, and cash AONIA rose from 4.35 to 4.60. Equities and VIX treated landing as benign. The seat closed because new AU risk was blocked and a hike-path receive was anti-defensive into unverified demand. AU is eligible now; the remaining strip-to-cash gap is 31bp.
causal.original_belief: Receiving the Mar-Jun 2027 AONIA average at 4.91 versus cash 4.35 was a defensive fade of too much hiking: Australian demand would fail and the strip would print lower.
causal.same_information_counterfactual: With AU blocked and a benign risk tape, standing down or paying the strip would have avoided the loss. The 2026-09-30 close was the right reaction to that information. Re-entering a Jun27 receive now is not implied: cash has already moved 25bp toward the strip and only 31bp remains.

postmortems.expression_assessment: Receiving a hike-priced Mar-Jun 2027 average was a fade of tightening, not a slowdown hedge. That vehicle conflicted with the defensive remit once demand was unverified and risk assets were bid. The close was process-correct; the open was the error.
postmortems.future_rule: If cash sits below the policy-path strip and risk assets treat landing as benign, do not receive that strip as a defensive expression. Sit out, pay the strip if the view is stress, or receive only a tenor where tightening is already extreme in the price.
postmortems.lesson: A receive of a STIR or policy-path strip that prices hikes while cash is still below that strip is a fade of tightening, not a defensive slowdown trade.
postmortems.thesis_assessment: The view that Jun27 AONIA at 4.91 would fall because demand would fail was not borne out. Cash rose; the strip did not.
postmortems.what_failed: Opening a receive of a 2027 hike average as a defensive trade. The strip never came in, cash tightened, and the book lost 12718.75 over about ten days.
postmortems.what_worked: Closing when Australia was blocked and the hike-path receive was recognized as anti-defensive. The 4.91 mark did not run against the book while cash rose 25bp after the exit.

Timing on the rates and FX event is uncertain, so linear spot and cash rates are the wrong expression versus bounded-risk convexity. Book stays flat; no invented vol, strike, or premium.

reasons: Original belief (defensive receive vs cash gap) is stated and contrasted with observed reality (flat strip, cash +25bp, loss, process-correct close).

deployment_hurdle.benchmark: Official NY Fed SOFR ACT/360 3.88% as of 2026-09-29 charged on shocked-risk capital; stay flat if expected edge does not cover that charge after a plausible adverse 100bp rate move.

Canada official curve beyond CORRA tape prints
FX forward points and AUDUSD basis
candidate_assessments.rationale: Mark is 4.91 against AONIA cash 4.60, so 31bp of tightening is already in the curve. Paying duration expects a still-higher mark, but the residual does not cover official SOFR 3.88% ACT/360 on shocked risk capital after a 100bp adverse easing path, and carry is negative if cash remains near 4.60.

deployment_hurdle.chosen_action_rationale: The only expanding markable handoff is pay AONIA_2027-06. It is evaluable and fails the SOFR-on-shocked-capital hurdle. A flat book therefore stays flat.

grinder.invalidation: Reopen a pay only if June 2027 implied AONIA cheapens toward cash while inflation, oil, or the cash rate itself is clearly repricing higher, so expected edge would cover official SOFR charged on shocked risk capital after a plausible 100 basis-point adverse move.
grinder.thesis: June 2027 Australian overnight is already 4.91 versus 4.60 cash, so a new pay needs implied rates to rise further after 31 basis points of tightening have been priced. Firm oil and a high global rate backdrop can support a hawkish bias, but that residual is too thin against negative carry if cash stays near 4.60 and against a 100 basis-point easing shock on new risk capital. Stay flat.

expression_memo.rationale: No incremental rates or spot risk; managing the current book only.

pragmatist.invalidation: The receive is wrong if March CORRA implied reclaims 3.13 and keeps rising as cash and the 2027 strip reprice a genuine hiking cycle, especially with oil holding above 100 and a further US front-end backup dragging Canada with it.

portfolio_construction.adverse_scenario: Oil stays bid near 100 and US yields remain at cycle highs, forcing a Bank of Canada catch-up. March CORRA implied rises from 3.09 back through 3.13 toward the rest of the 2027 strip (3.34 June / 3.515 September), hitting the receive on both mark and carry.

candidate_interactions.rationale: A pay-Australia line would make money in the same global-hawkish / oil-spillover shock that hurts the Canada receive, so it is a theoretical offset rather than duplicate Canada beta. At the handed-off 25 million size versus 450 million CORRA it is not a material diversifier.

portfolio_construction.chosen_actions_rationale: Hold the working 450 million CORRA receive. The line is through entry, cash is still 2.30, and Canada-US yield divergence remains the clean opportunistic expression. The 25 million AONIA pay is rejected as economically irrelevant to the adverse path.
portfolio_construction.existing_book_summary: Single live line: long/receive 450 million CORRA March 2027, entry 3.13, implied 3.09, shocked risk capital 4.5 million, drawdown 252342.50 versus the hard stop. The book is a Canada-easing / overpriced-hike-path expression versus 2.30 cash CORRA.

independent_handoff_opportunities.rationale: Only accepted expanding ticket: short/pay AONIA June 2027 at 4.91 versus 4.60 cash, Australia eligible, expecting the mark higher if more tightening is delivered than the 31bp already in the contract.

rejected_complements.reason: Twenty-five million of June AONIA pay is noise versus 450 million March CORRA and would not change shocked P&L in the oil/US-spillover scenario. Upsizing it would import a second hawkish-duration bet that fights the core receive-Canada thesis.

pragmatist.thesis: Keep the Canada receive. Cash CORRA at 2.30 still sits 79bp below the March 2027 implied 3.09, so the live line continues to be paid to fade a Bank of Canada catch-up that has not appeared in the policy rate even while US yields sit at a multi-decade high. Canada 10-year yields near 3.96 have not tracked the US 10-year, which is the core divergence, and a token Australia pay does not change oil-and-US-spillover risk on a 450 million receive.

expression_memo.rationale: No incremental rates or spot risk; managing the current book only.

swinger.invalidation: Reduce or close if March 2027 implied CORRA pushes through 3.25–3.30 on an actual Bank of Canada hike or a clear catch-up to the global tightening impulse, because that would mean the 2.30-to-3.09 gap was the start of the path rather than a misprice.
swinger.thesis: Keep receiving March 2027 CORRA as a single concentrated line. Cash is still 2.30 while the contract sits at 3.09, so the market is asking for about eighty basis points of Bank of Canada tightening into early spring; that remains too much path unless policy has already turned, and the payoff is a lower mark if hikes are delayed or scaled back. Size stays where it is: global yields at multi-decade highs and oil above one hundred are a live headwind, not a reason to press a book that already expresses the view.
